summary.value: The Whiting True Blue is a modern American laying breed, not a heritage one. Poultry geneticist Dr. Tom Whiting developed it in Colorado in the 1990s by crossing White Leghorns with Ameraucanas. He started out breeding for fly-tying feathers, and the birds turned out to be strong layers of blue eggs. Every True Blue lays a blue egg, while a sister line, the True Green, lays green ones. Feather colors vary widely, with chipmunk and gray patterns the most common. Hens lay about 280 to 300 large powder blue eggs a year. The birds are very active and do best on free range, where they eagerly hunt insects. Reports on their manner differ: one source calls them friendly and gentle, another says they are independent and slow to trust people unless handled young. They get along well with the rest of the flock.
